question.text: An AIF's minimum capital commitment from each investor is normally INR 1 crore. But the regulation carves out reduced thresholds. Which of the following is a CORRECT reduced minimum investment under the SEBI (AIF) Regulations?

answer.text: INR 25 lakh minimum for employees / directors of the AIF or Manager
INR 10 lakh minimum for any retail investor with CA attestation
INR 50 lakh minimum for NRIs investing via NRO account
INR 2 crore minimum for foreign portfolio investors (FPIs)

explanation.text: The Logic: The standard minimum investment per investor in an AIF is INR 1 crore, but employees and directors of the AIF or Manager may invest with a reduced floor of INR 25 lakh. The INR 1 crore minimum is not applicable to Accredited Investors, and Large Value Funds for Accredited Investors operate under separate flexibility. The Trap: Option B fabricates a retail floor. Option C invents an NRI carve-out that does not exist. Option D doubles the floor for FPIs. Note: The employee/director carve-out exists so that those running the fund can hold meaningful skin in the game without facing the INR 1 crore floor.
